marketing_wrapper: Very heavy. All four images sit on a peach/blush gradient backdrop with big dark-brown captions. 01 is a faded, tinted map under a caption, a mock search field and 'Featured in Forbes / 4.8 Rating' badges: essentially marketing art. 02 is a review bubble, a caption, and a phone cropped to its top third showing a camera feed, with an enlarged 'Walk Signal' banner breaking out of the frame. 03 and 04 show a cropped phone with an Apple Maps route and an oversized banner card overflowing the frame. Real UI is about 30-45% of each image, and the banner cards are staged at enlarged size.

typography.display: SF Pro bold in banners ('Walk Signal', 'Signal ahead', '730 ft'); captions also bold SF Pro in dark brown
typography.body: system SF (secondary lines in regular grey)
typography.weights: Bold/semibold primary line, regular secondary line

palette.accent_strategy: Semantic only: green full-bleed banner for Walk, yellow tint and warning triangle for 'Signal ahead', orange route line and location dot. The peach/blush gradient is marketing backdrop.
palette.source: palette.json 01-04 (#fbe3da, #fed5c5, #fff2f0 = marketing peach backdrop; #f4eee3 / #ddd9d2 = Apple Maps base), 02 (#6b7a5c/#84ac86 green banner region); route orange and warning yellow matched visually

shape.radius_language: large ~20pt banner cards; circular icon badge; diamond road-sign glyph
shape.borders_shadows: Banners carry soft glows/shadows (likely marketing enlargement); yellow banner has a pale yellow rim
shape.materials: flat cards over MapKit and a live camera feed

density: low: one instruction banner over a full-screen map or camera view
layout: Full-screen camera feed (signal detection) or Apple Maps route view with a single large status/instruction banner at the top.
navigation: Not visible: no tab bar or nav bar appears in any frame.
imagery_and_icons: Live camera feed; Apple Maps (MapKit) basemap; SF Symbols-style walking figure, warning triangle, turn-left diamond sign
signature_visual_move: A single oversized, colour-coded status banner (green walk, yellow caution) sitting over the camera or map view.

direction_fit.secondary: Glance Board (one status at a time, semantic colour)
direction_fit.why: Screenshots can't show haptics or audio, which is where the text record puts the direction. What is visible is a minimal, high-contrast, one-state-at-a-time banner over native map and camera views, consistent with a screen that is secondary to sound and haptics.

notes: Too marketing-heavy to judge chrome, density or navigation. The listing now leads with 'Navigate confidently with AI' and a review quote, a marketing shift away from the accessibility framing. Visual evidence is not enough for the direction; it needs device capture with VoiceOver and haptics.
